descriptors.definition: An item meeting the definition of an intangible asset is recognized when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and its cost can be measured reliably. Subsequent expenditures are generally recognized in profit or loss as incurred unless they specifically enhance an existing asset.
inclusion: costs incurred initially to acquire or internally generate an intangible asset
subsequent expenditures that add to, replace part of, or service an existing intangible asset meeting criteria
exclusion: subsequent expenditure on brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and customer lists
expenditures that cannot be distinguished from developing the business as a whole
nearby_distinctions: Initial acquisition costs versus subsequent maintenance expenditures
Intangible assets versus general business development expenses

descriptors.concept_name: Recognition of Intangible Assets - General Principles
descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is recognized only if future economic benefits are probable and the cost can be reliably measured based on management's best estimates. Subsequent expenditures are rarely capitalized because they typically maintain existing benefits rather than create a new recognizable asset.
inclusion: initial acquisition costs
qualifying subsequent replacement costs
exclusion: subsequent expenditure on brands and customer lists
general business upkeep costs
nearby_distinctions: General recognition criteria versus specialized internal generation rules

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets are initially measured at cost upon acquisition or self-generation. Separately acquired assets automatically satisfy probability criteria and include purchase price and directly attributable preparation costs.
inclusion: purchase price including import duties and non-refundable taxes
employee benefits cost arising directly from bringing the asset to working condition
professional fees and testing costs
exclusion: general administrative overhead
costs incurred after asset is ready for intended use
nearby_distinctions: Initial cost measurement versus subsequent measurement models

descriptors.definition: Separately acquired intangible assets are measured at cost comprising purchase price and direct preparation expenses, with the probability criterion automatically considered satisfied. Capitalization ceases once the asset is capable of operating in the manner intended by management.
inclusion: cash price equivalent for deferred payments
costs of testing whether the asset works properly
exclusion: interest expense recognized over credit period
costs incurred after cessation of capitalization
nearby_distinctions: Separate acquisition cost components versus business combination fair value measurement

descriptors.concept_name: Acquisition as Part of a Business Combination
descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired in a business combination are measured at fair value at the acquisition date, which incorporates market expectations of future economic benefits. The acquirer recognizes these identifiable assets separately from goodwill even if the acquiree had not previously recognized them.
inclusion: identifiable intangible assets arising from contractual or legal rights
in-process research and development projects meeting asset definitions
exclusion: goodwill components not meeting identifiable asset criteria
nearby_distinctions: Business combination fair value recognition versus separate acquisition historical cost

descriptors.concept_name: Acquisition by Way of a Government Grant
descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired free of charge or for nominal consideration via government grants are recognized initially at fair value or at a nominal amount plus direct preparation costs. Asset exchanges are measured at fair value unless the transaction lacks commercial substance or fair values are unreliable.
inclusion: airport landing rights and radio licenses
assets received in commercial exchanges measured at fair value
exclusion: exchanges lacking commercial substance measured at fair value
nearby_distinctions: Government grant nominal recognition versus standard fair value acquisition

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired in exchange for other assets are measured at fair value unless the transaction lacks commercial substance or fair values cannot be measured reliably. If fair value is not used, the cost is measured at the carrying amount of the asset given up.
inclusion: assets acquired via exchange of non-monetary or mixed assets
reliable fair value measurements of received or given assets
exclusion: transactions lacking significant changes in future cash flow configurations
nearby_distinctions: Exchange valuation using fair value versus carrying amount of asset given up

descriptors.definition: Internally generated goodwill is prohibited from recognition as an asset because it lacks an identifiable, separable resource controlled by the entity with a reliably measurable cost. Discrepancies between an entity's fair value and its net identifiable assets do not represent recognizable intangible asset costs.
inclusion: unrecognized business value drivers contributing to overall corporate worth
exclusion: recognized goodwill arising strictly from business combinations
identifiable intangible assets separately acquired
nearby_distinctions: Prohibited internally generated goodwill versus acquired goodwill in business combinations

descriptors.definition: The generation of an internal intangible asset is split into a research phase and a development phase to determine recognition eligibility. Expenditures incurred during the research phase must be expensed immediately as no asset can be demonstrated to exist at that stage.
inclusion: original investigation activities aimed at obtaining new knowledge
search for alternative materials and processes
exclusion: development phase expenditures meeting strict capitalization criteria
internally generated brands, mastheads, and customer lists
nearby_distinctions: Research phase immediate expensing versus development phase capitalization criteria

descriptors.definition: Expenditures on intangible items are recognized as expenses when incurred unless they form part of a recognized intangible asset cost or business combination goodwill. Specific outlays like research, start-up costs, training, advertising, and relocation must always be expensed.
inclusion: establishment and pre-opening costs
advertising and promotional expenditures
training and reorganization costs
exclusion: expenditures forming part of the cost of a qualifying intangible asset
prepayments for goods or services before rights are obtained
nearby_distinctions: Immediate expense recognition versus capitalization into intangible asset carrying amounts

descriptors.definition: Entities must choose either the cost model or the revaluation model as an accounting policy for subsequent measurement of intangible assets. Under the cost model, assets are carried at cost less accumulated amortization and impairment, whereas the revaluation model uses fair value based on active markets.
inclusion: carrying amount adjustments for amortization and impairment
fair value revaluations referenced to an active market
exclusion: initial recognition of unrecognized intangible assets via revaluation
selective revaluation of isolated assets without revaluing their entire class
nearby_distinctions: Cost model carrying value tracking versus active market revaluation model

descriptors.definition: Following initial recognition, an intangible asset is accounted for using the cost model by carrying it at cost less any accumulated amortisation and any accumulated impairment losses. This model forms the baseline measurement approach unless the revaluation model option is elected for an entire class of assets.
inclusion: historical cost less amortisation and impairment adjustments
exclusion: fair value adjustments without an active market revaluation policy
nearby_distinctions: Cost model historical tracking versus revaluation model fair value adjustments
